title: Measuring emergence in bits
claim: For a nonempty relation R on n bits, with pair closure pc(R) (points whose every two-coordinate projection occurs in R): (1) the logical emergence E(R) = log2|pc(R)| - log2|R| is zero exactly when R is majority-closed, that is, definable by clauses of at most two literals; (2) a knot on N bits is the complement of a nonempty independent set Z of the N-cube and has E = -log2(1 - |Z|/2^N) <= 1, with equality only for the two parity relations (34, 742 and 254,474 knots on 3, 4 and 5 bits); (3) the statistical emergence I(R), the divergence of the uniform distribution on R from the pairwise exponential family, satisfies 0 <= I <= E and vanishes exactly on least sets of pairwise energies, so the four not-all-equal relations are the only knots with I = 0; (4) the largest E on n bits is n - log2 CAN(2,n,2), attained by minimum covering arrays; (5) I <= min(n, |R| - 1) - log2|R| <= n - log2(n+1), with equality exactly for orthogonal arrays of strength two with n + 1 runs (Hadamard designs), which on seven bits are the 480 cosets of the Fano simplex codes; (6) affine relations have I = E <= n - ceil(log2(n+1)); E and I add over products.
failure_conditions: A relation on at most four bits where zero logical emergence and majority closure differ.
A knot on three or four bits that is not the complement of an independent set, or whose emergence differs from -log2(1 - |Z|/2^N), or a one-bit knot other than parity.

A three-bit relation where zero statistical emergence and least-set membership differ, where I falls outside [0, E], or a silent knot other than not-all-equal; a sampled four-bit knot that is a least set.
A relation on at most four bits, or one with at most five points on five bits, above n - log2 CAN(n); a failure of the capacity inequality for 6 <= n <= 5000.
A relation exceeding min(n, |R| - 1) - log2|R|, or an 8-point set on seven bits with uniform pairs outside the 480 simplex cosets.
A subspace on at most six bits with all pairs free and codimension above n - ceil(log2(n+1)).
foundation_claim_scope: Two measures of how much a relation on bits hides from its pairs, their zero sets and their maxima. No native recurrence beyond the K1-K3 reading, no space, no physics.

validation.status: checked: prose proof; check.py decides zero emergence on all 65,805 relations on two to four bits, the knot classification on three and four bits and the independent sets of the 5-cube, statistical emergence on all 255 three-bit relations with exact rational linear programming, the capacities exhaustively on at most four bits, on small five-bit relations, by construction to ten bits and by the proof inequality to n = 5000, the 480 seven-bit maximizers by clique search, and all subspaces on at most six bits; five controls rejected; no human or external review
validation.level: V1 prose proof with exhaustive and exact checks; Baker and Pixley, Schaefer, the closure of exponential families, Rauh-Kahle-Ay, Kleitman-Spencer and Katona, Hadamard-orthogonal-array correspondence and the Hamming bound are cited; no trusted kernel.
validation.novelty: known-overlap-found for the zero sets (majority closure; facial sets); candidate-local-delta for the two capacity theorems for relations (covering arrays; Hadamard designs, with the 480 Fano maximizers on seven bits), the statistically silent knots, and the reading of both measures as emergence. Bounded search: Rauh 2011 and Matus-Ay study maximizers of divergence from exponential families over all distributions.
validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-10-21.
